# Results — Leakage-Aware & Explainable ML/DL Framework for UPI Fraud Detection

*Auto-generated by `make_report.py` from `reports/tables/`. Test set = 5,374 transactions
from 964 users never seen in training. Thresholds are chosen on validation only.*
*Full run: 3 deep-learning seeds, 12 tuning iterations per classical model, runtime 13.0 min.*

## 1. Dataset & audit
- 26,393 transactions, 4,818 users, 65 raw columns, fraud rate 17.2%. No duplicates.
- `timestamp` holds only `MM:SS.f` (no date / hour) → chronological split impossible; replaced by a **user-grouped split** (0 users shared across train / val / test).
- **Label proxies:** `handle_verification_status` (AUC 1.000), `receiver_account_age` (AUC 0.993), `receiver_transaction_history` (AUC 0.947).
- **Scenario signatures:** 39 columns take a single value for *every* legitimate transaction; any other value implies fraud.
- **Interaction leak:** `geographic_disparity` and `geographic_location_vs_ip` are exactly equal in 100 % of legitimate rows but only
  36 % of fraud rows (AUC of their absolute difference 0.821), although each column alone has AUC ≈ 0.50.
  It was first noticed because the MLP's Integrated-Gradients ranking put these "useless" columns at the top; a pairwise-equality check then confirmed it.
  The pair is excluded from the strict Tier 2 set.

## 2. Experiment 1 — leakage inflates performance
| model | setting | n_features | pr_auc | roc_auc | precision | recall | f1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic Regression | T0_all_features | 49 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| XGBoost | T0_all_features | 49 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| MLP | T0_all_features | 49 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| Logistic Regression | T1_proxies_removed | 46 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| XGBoost | T1_proxies_removed | 46 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| MLP | T1_proxies_removed | 46 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.999 | 1.000 |
| Logistic Regression | T2a_behavioural_with_geo_pair | 14 | 0.868 | 0.918 | 0.894 | 0.752 | 0.817 |
| XGBoost | T2a_behavioural_with_geo_pair | 14 | 0.949 | 0.967 | 0.985 | 0.873 | 0.925 |
| MLP | T2a_behavioural_with_geo_pair | 14 | 0.941 | 0.963 | 0.989 | 0.857 | 0.918 |
| Logistic Regression | T2_behavioural | 12 | 0.868 | 0.918 | 0.895 | 0.753 | 0.818 |
| XGBoost | T2_behavioural | 12 | 0.948 | 0.969 | 0.986 | 0.876 | 0.928 |
| MLP | T2_behavioural | 12 | 0.938 | 0.961 | 0.984 | 0.853 | 0.914 |
| Rule baseline | T2_behavioural (range rule) | 12 | 0.851 | 0.914 | 0.988 | 0.831 | 0.903 |

**Finding:** with all features, or with only the 3 label proxies removed, every model is (near-)*perfect*. This is
leakage, not skill. Adding back the geographic pair (T2a) gives XGBoost 0.949 and MLP 0.941;
on the 12 strict behavioural features the scores are 0.868 (LR),
0.948 (XGBoost) and 0.938 (MLP).
A transparent rule that learns only the legitimate min/max of each feature reaches precision 0.988 / recall 0.831.

In the random row split 96% of test rows belong to users already seen in training.
The difference to the grouped split is small, i.e. in this synthetic data fraud is not tied to user identity; the grouped split is kept because
it is the methodologically correct choice for real data.

## 6. Experiment 2 — main model comparison (tuned)
| model | setting | val_pr_auc | pr_auc | pr_auc_ci_low | pr_auc_ci_high | roc_auc | precision | recall | f1 | fp | fn | hard_subset_pr_auc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic Regression | T2 tuned | 0.846 | 0.868 | 0.851 | 0.886 | 0.918 | 0.896 | 0.753 | 0.818 | 84 | 237 | 0.240 |
| Random Forest | T2 tuned | 0.934 | 0.949 | 0.937 | 0.959 | 0.971 | 0.975 | 0.876 | 0.923 | 22 | 119 | 0.403 |
| XGBoost | T2 tuned | 0.937 | 0.953 | 0.943 | 0.963 | 0.974 | 0.983 | 0.879 | 0.928 | 15 | 116 | 0.432 |
| MLP | T2 | 0.929 | 0.942 | 0.930 | 0.953 | 0.965 | 0.982 | 0.857 | 0.915 | 15 | 137 | 0.390 |
| LSTM | T2 sequences (k=5) | 0.920 | 0.930 | 0.917 | 0.943 | 0.953 | 0.976 | 0.834 | 0.899 | 20 | 159 | 0.344 |
| Rule baseline | range rule |  | 0.851 |  |  | 0.914 | 0.988 | 0.831 | 0.903 | 10 | 162 |  |

- **Champion (best validation PR-AUC): XGBoost**, test PR-AUC 0.953 (95 % user-bootstrap CI 0.943–0.963),
  precision 0.983, recall 0.879, 15 false alarms and 116 missed frauds out of 959.
- Deep learning: MLP PR-AUC 0.942, LSTM 0.930 — competitive but not better than gradient boosting on tabular data.
- **Hard subset** (4,567 test rows, 162 frauds, prevalence 3.5%) where every feature lies inside the
  legitimate range: PR-AUC drops to 0.240–0.432. Most of the "easy" detection comes from
  out-of-range values produced by the synthetic generator; the hard subset is the honest measure of learned behaviour.

McNemar tests (champion vs others, test decisions):
| champion | versus | a_right_b_wrong | a_wrong_b_right | p_value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| XGBoost | Logistic Regression | 210 | 20 | 0.000 |
| XGBoost | Random Forest | 18 | 8 | 0.078 |
| XGBoost | MLP | 30 | 9 | 0.001 |
| XGBoost | LSTM | 63 | 15 | 0.000 |

## 7. Experiment 6 — MLP vs LSTM, does order matter?
| model | setting | pr_auc_mean | pr_auc_std | roc_auc_mean | recall_mean | precision_mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLP | current transaction only (T2) | 0.940 | 0.003 | 0.962 | 0.856 | 0.981 |
| MLP | current + history aggregates (T2H) | 0.937 | 0.001 | 0.959 | 0.854 | 0.972 |
| LSTM | sequence length 1 (no history) | 0.940 | 0.000 | 0.960 | 0.862 | 0.983 |
| LSTM | last 5 transactions, ordered | 0.933 | 0.003 | 0.955 | 0.847 | 0.965 |
| LSTM | last 5 transactions, history shuffled | 0.929 | 0.003 | 0.953 | 0.834 | 0.974 |

- Ordered vs shuffled history: 0.933 vs 0.929 → **transaction order carries
  no measurable signal**.
- LSTM with sequence length 1: 0.940 vs length 5: 0.933 → earlier transactions
  do not help. Consistent with a generator that labels each transaction
  independently of the user's history. With real, dated UPI data this experiment should be repeated.

## 8. Experiment 7 — explainability
Top-5 features — XGBoost SHAP: request_amount_roundness, amount, transaction_time_of_day, keyboard_input_speed, transaction_amount_vs_sender_history; MLP Integrated Gradients:
request_amount_roundness, amount, transaction_time_of_day, input_timing_consistency, transaction_amount_vs_sender_history; LSTM permutation: amount, request_amount_roundness, input_timing_consistency, transaction_time_of_day, input_pause_patterns.
Spearman rank agreement SHAP vs IG: **ρ = 0.811**.

**Explanations as a leakage detector (Exp 7b).** Training default XGBoost and MLP on the same split, the SHAP-vs-IG rank agreement is
ρ = 0.473 *with* the leaky geographic pair (IG top-3: request_amount_roundness, amount, geographic_disparity)
and ρ = 0.832 *without* it. The neural network latched onto the jointly-leaky pair that the trees used differently;
disagreement between explanation methods was the first visible symptom of the interaction leak.

| feature | shap_rank | ig_rank |
|---|---|---|
| request_amount_roundness | 1 | 1 |
| amount | 2 | 2 |
| transaction_time_of_day | 3 | 3 |
| keyboard_input_speed | 4 | 10 |
| transaction_amount_vs_sender_history | 5 | 5 |
| input_timing_consistency | 6 | 4 |
| input_pause_patterns | 7 | 7 |
| session_duration | 8 | 8 |
| background_data_usage | 9 | 6 |
| screen_active_time | 10 | 11 |
| pin_entry_speed | 11 | 9 |
| app_switching_frequency | 12 | 12 |

## 9. Answers to the research questions
1. **How much does leakage inflate performance?** From PR-AUC ≈1.000 to 0.948 (XGBoost) / 0.868 (LR) once
   proxies and scenario signatures are removed, and to ≈0.43 on the hard subset.
2. **Which model performs best after the audit?** XGBoost (validation-selected). McNemar: significantly better than
   Logistic Regression, MLP, LSTM (p < 0.05); not significantly different from Random Forest.
3. **Class weights vs SMOTE?** Small differences once the threshold is tuned; imbalance (17 %) is moderate.
4. **Can SHAP explain flagged transactions?** Yes — per-transaction SHAP is shown in the dashboard (ρ between SHAP and IG rankings =
   0.811). Explainability also served as an *audit tool*: IG exposed the geographic interaction leak.
5. **Does sequence modelling help?** Not on this dataset: order and history add no signal; documented as a data limitation.

## 10. Limitations
- Synthetic data with deterministic scenario injection; results do not transfer to real UPI traffic.
- No usable dates → no temporal validation; LSTM order is an intra-day pseudo-chronology.
- Cost analysis uses assumed costs (₹100 per alert, ₹1,000 per false alarm).
- Feature importance shows what a model uses, not what causes fraud.
